names.pullman_house_1729_prairie_ranges: 1729 Prairie Avenue — the Pullman estate's stable and one-storey ranges

source.citation: Inland Architect Press. Palm House and Stable of George M. Pullman, Chicago. S. S. Beman, Architect. Photographic plate in The Inland Architect and News Record, vol. 24, no. 1 (1894). Art Institute of Chicago, Ryerson and Burnham Archives, Archival Image Collection (Inland Architect plates).
what_it_supplies: the stable's forms: the arcade's three arches, the polygonal bay and its round-headed lights, the upper storey's wall and lights, the roof's west end springing from the first-floor cornice, the deck's cresting and the lantern
the belvedere's form: a square tower with a cornice and balustrade over the range's parapet
